messages:
Kira: flagging a subtle behaviour we hit in a tenant migration: hosted routing applied "prefer_low_cost" policy and bounced a private-tenant request to a quantized model variant that didn't support kv_cache_v2. Result: higher latency + correctness regression. We need clearer capability negotiation + routing priorities.
Tom: ugh. That's the classic policy mismatch. Two quick options: encode hard capabilities on the route (route_requires=[kv_cache_v2]) or add a routing predicate that checks 'capabilities.superset(route.requires)'.
Lina: I like predicates, but we also need an operator-facing fallback plan. If predicates fail, we should have deterministic fallback order and cost/latency signal so product owners can see tradeoffs.
Kira: +1 on operator visibility. Suggest we surface a "fallback_reason" in traces and in the Console UI with fields: attempted_route, matched_capabilities, fallback_chain, cost_delta_estimate.
Tom: also consider a soft vs hard requirement flag on routes. soft_requirement -> allow fallback with penalty tag; hard_requirement -> reject. Example route JSON: 
```
{
  "route": "/generate",
  "requires": ["kv_cache_v2"],
  "requirement": "soft"
}
```
This way we don't silently degrade correctness for hard requirements.
Lina: tradeoff: hard requirements reduce available capacity and may increase 429s under load. We need admission controls: quota buffers for hard routes or preemption policies.
Kira: yes. For Dedicated and Private tenants we should allow pinning: "pin_to_variant":"exact" to avoid routing surprises. Hosted tenants get the policy system.
Tom: question about capability evolution: how do we avoid schema explosion? I'd prefer versioned capability groups, e.g., cap_group:"cache-v1" with subfeatures, rather than dozens of boolean flags.
Lina: agree. cap_group also lets us do compatibility rules: group v2 is backwards-compatible with v1 but enables new optimizations. Controlplane can map groups to runtime features.
infra-bot: notice: maintenance window scheduled 2025-01-12T02:00Z for runtime that may affect model variants routing.
Kira: ops note: when fallback happens, we should emit a billing marker so customers can be charged appropriately for the higher-cost path and we can aggregate cost-impact metrics. Console should show per-tenant "fallback cost" in last-30-days.
Tom: implementation plan draft: (1) introduce capability groups + mapping (owner: Tom), (2) route requirement semantics (soft/hard/pinned) and admission controls (owner: Lina), (3) trace/fallback_reason and billing markers (owner: Kira).
Lina: metric thresholds: if >3% of requests for a tenant fall back in a 10m window, trigger "fallback spike" alert; if fallback causes correctness regressions flagged by evals, auto-halt new rollouts. I will add alert drafts.
Kira: timelines? Can we prototype the trace field + simple route flag in 10 business days?
Tom: reasonable. I'll mock the cap_group mapping and a minimal routing predicate by EOD tomorrow for the RFC.
Lina: I'll wire alerts with a fake metric stream for now.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary routing for route=/generate pinned=false will run 2024-12-02T20:00Z in us-west1.
Kira: note: don't start canary until cap_group mapping exists or we'll get noisy fallbacks. Please hold.
Tom: acknowledged, will hold canary until we have at least the trace field and mapping in place.
Kira: thanks everyone. I'll open a short RFC PR with the example route JSON and trace spec. Post comments here if you want changes.
